# Historical Decomposition

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

theta_0 <- matrix(rnorm(10, 0, 1), ncol=2, nrow= 5)
irf_response_test <- as.data.frame(theta_0)
irf_response_test$shock <- rep(names, length.out = length(theta_0[,1]))
irf_response_test$shock <- factor(irf_response_test$shock, levels = rev(names))
# fake plot just to construct the correct legend
dates_formatted <- as.yearmon(time(x))
dates_formatted <- dates_formatted[5:length(dates_formatted)]
# Format to shorter labels (e.g., "May 15", "Jun 15", ...)

str(dates_formatted)
colors_shock <- c("blue", "red", "green", "yellow")
names <- c("$Q_{elec}$" ,"$P_{elec}$", "IPI",  "$NE Index$")

plot_legend <- ggplot(data =irf_response_test, aes(x=V1, fill = shock))+
  geom_histogram()+
  theme( legend.direction = "horizontal")+
scale_fill_manual(
  values = rev(colors_shock),
  labels = TeX(rev(names)))
# Légende personnalisée (à ajuster selon vos besoins)
custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot_legend)
plot_legend
```

La différence qui existe entre ma série et la série reconstruite
correspond à l'approximation de la limite des horizons.
Lorsque pour une Cholesky, on calcule de plus en plus d'horizons,
la différence entre les deux courbes se réduit
En plus, il y avait la dérive intuitée par Giovanni.


```{r}

zero_errors <- matrix(0, nrow = dim(res)[1], ncol = dim(res)[2])

reconstruct_derive_without_errors <- iterate_var_ter(initial_obs = x[1:4, ],
                                                     errors = zero_errors,
                                                     var_model = vl)

# Prepare data for plotting

plot_hd <- function(series){
  
  decomp_tot_data <- data.frame(
    time= dates_formatted,
    historical_decomp_matrix[,series,])
  # Plot the decomposition
  colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1] <- names

  # Reshaper les données en format long pour ggplot2
  library(tidyr)
  long_data <- pivot_longer(decomp_tot_data, 
                            cols = -time, names_to = "category",
                            values_to = "value")
  # S'assurer que 'category' a l'ordre des niveaux correspondant à 'colors_shock'
  long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = names)
  
  # Tracer des barres empilées avec ggplot2
  my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= long_data, aes(x = time, y = value, fill = category),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack") +  # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = colors_shock,
      labels = TeX(names))+
    #scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red", "green"), labels = c("Supply", "Demand", "Other")) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  comparison <- lag(as.vector(vars_demeaned[5:96,series]), 20)
  comparison[1:20] <- rep(vars_demeaned[4,series], 10)
  
  
  data <- data.frame(
    x = dates_formatted,
    y = vars_demeaned[5:nrow(vars_demeaned),series] - reconstruct_derive_without_errors$NE_Index_log[c(-1:-p)],
    ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum)
  )
  
  my_plot <- my_plot + 
    geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y), linetype = "dashed") +  # Add dashed line+
    geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = ytest), linetype = "dashed", color='grey') +
    labs(title=TeX(paste("Historical Decomposition of",names[[series]])) ,
         x="Time", y="Contribution")
  return(my_plot)
}

historical_decomp_matrix <- hd_cholesky
plot_hd(series = 4)
```
Describing the summation Error

```{r}
data <- data.frame(
  x = dates_formatted,
  y = vars_demeaned[5:nrow(vars_demeaned),series],
  ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum)
)


ggplot(data, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = y, color = "Actual")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ytest, color = "Decomposition")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = y- ytest, color = "Error")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual" = "blue", 
                                "Decomposition" = "red",
                                "Error"="black")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = paste("Decomposition of", series, "using historical data"),
       x = "Date",
       y = "Value") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Montrer le terme de dérive lorsqu'on fait tourner la VAR sans erreurs


```{r}


ggplot() +
  geom_line(mapping= aes(x= dates_formatted, 
                         y = reconstruct_derive_without_errors$NE_Index_log[c(-1:-p)], color = "Derive"))+
  geom_line(data=data, mapping=aes(x = x, y = y - ytest, color = "Error")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Derive" = "blue", 
                                "Decomposition" = "red",
                                "Error"="black")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = paste("Decomposition of", series, "using historical data"),
       x = "Date",
       y = "Value") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```



```{r}

# Apply the function to the sequence 3:10
results <- lapply(c(1:n) , plot_hd)

# Arrange the plots in a grid
plots_grid <- do.call("grid.arrange", c(results, nrow = 2))

# Combine the grid with the legend
final_plot <- plot_grid(plots_grid, custom_legend, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))

title <- ggdraw() + 
  draw_label(TeX('Historical Decomposition'), fontface = 'bold', x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)

# Combine the title and the final plot with legend
final_plot_with_title <- plot_grid(title, final_plot, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1))

# Display the final plot
print(final_plot_with_title)
```
